persons.name: Holly Madison
persons.harm: Moved into the Playboy Mansion as one of the founder's live-in girlfriends; sexually coerced on her first night while heavily intoxicated, then subjected to years of control (curfew, banned from working, rules), triangulation, surveillance by his security, unpaid labour on the TV show, and verbal and emotional abuse.
persons.perpetrator_role: her much older live-in boyfriend, the Playboy founder

quotes.quote: And people think that's a little strange because I talk about a situation where boundaries were crossed. And people assume you would just want to run away from that. But I didn't have anywhere to live.
it was always super important to me when I was talking about [perpetrator] to the press to Say really positive things not only because I cared about him But because I didn't want to get in trouble
In the beginning, I fell for it, hook line and sinker. I thought the problem was all the other women.

persons.outcome_quote: I left, and it was emotionally harrowing for me because I did feel very, very guilty. He had trained me well.
persons.notes: The perpetrator is referred to on air by transcribed forms of his nickname; not recorded here. The only institution-like contact was Holly going to his secretary's office with receipts about being unpaid for the TV show (@44:39-45:42; the secretary 'called somebody and made something happen'); this concerned pay, not the sexual/emotional abuse, so it is not coded as the harm reaching an institution. The production company (the show) is an employer-like body but the abuse was not raised with it. Holly also mentions going 'straight from one really controlling relationship to another' (next boyfriend, security following her, @61:08) but the season tells nothing further, so no separate record. Family were not told: 'I'm not comfortable talking about anything like that with my family, so they didn't know.' (@24:58).

(@11:26); 'He consulted with an HR lawyer... you can go to your appointments but not on company time.' (@26:00). Outcome is partly_protected because the employer's attendance restrictions contributed to 'the walls closing in' but the colleague left by quitting; no licensing action was possible (see Alice). Forged signatures led Naomi to monitor her credit for a year (E4 @44:31).

coder_notes: All eight chunk files read in full to their stated last lines. The season folder contains 13 numbered episodes plus two unnumbered 'WCN Presents SWW S15 E5 Updates' episodes (Diana), which I treated as part of the season. E10-E11 update Season 9 (Danielle) and E13 updates Season 7 (Amy B. Chesler); persons from those updates are coded from what these episodes say only, so their institutional histories are incomplete. E12 is an expert episode (Consent Awareness Network); the public-figure examples (Andrea Constand, Jennifer Siebel Newsom) and the TEDx Purdue case are coded with low confidence and could be treated as bare mentions. Perpetrator names (including show pseudonyms) are replaced with [perpetrator] in quotations; non-harmed people quoted verbatim (e.g. the agency owner's first name) are left as spoken because the instructions say to change nothing else in a quotation. Where a quote crosses a timestamp marker the source gives the marker where the passage begins. Valentina's 'decisive work' quote begins at 22:44 and continues into 23:48. Unassigned: only titles that could plausibly touch Season 15 themes were opened; none referred to Season 15 people. Work was interrupted several times by usage limits; notes.md was kept after every file and the JSON was built from it.
